chief_complaint: Advanced chronic kidney disease (stage 4) awaiting transplantation, with diabetes mellitus, hypertension, ischemic heart disease and multiple comorbidities requiring complex management.
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 104‑year‑old woman with a lifelong history of type 2 diabetes (since 1977) and essential hypertension (since 1967) that have progressed to advanced diabetic kidney disease (CKD stage 4, onset 2022) and non‑proliferative diabetic retinopathy (2022). She is on the transplant waiting list (2022). Cardiovascular disease is extensive: myocardial infarction (1990), coronary artery bypass graft (1994) and ongoing ischemic heart disease managed with antiplatelet agents, beta‑blockers, ACE‑inhibitor, nitrates and statins. Alzheimer’s disease (1996) contributes to medication adherence challenges. She also has obesity, metabolic syndrome, hypertriglyceridemia, hyperglycemia, and a history of brain injury (2019). Dental issues (impacted molars, loss of teeth) and recent oral imaging raise infection risk. Socially, she reports intimate‑partner abuse, unsatisfactory housing, a criminal record and full‑time employment, all of which complicate care. Polypharmacy is high (14 agents) with duplicate and atypical prescriptions (e.g., chronic alteplase).
